**What's wrong**

A custom provider whose key is locked to one protocol (`keyProtocol: "anthropic"`) but whose only URL is an OpenAI-compatible one (`chat: https://…/v1`) keeps serving requests — routing has fallen back to the URLs the provider has since #1702 — yet `magpie provider test` (and the provider page's Test) answers the chat endpoint with

```
  ✗ chat       no key is on for this endpoint
```

so the one surface meant to tell you what traffic does says the opposite of what traffic does. And with the lock set, the terminal has no way back: `magpie provider key <id> <key>` keeps the stale protocol, `magpie provider set` takes no key-protocol pair, and the only remedy is editing `providers.json` by hand. Credit @xtnntn for the report and for pinning the frontend comment against the runtime behavior.

**Root cause**

The gateway plans this provider whole on the URLs it has (`perKeyEvery`'s no-URL candidate, `TestKeyForAProtocolWithNoURLIsSaid` covers the wire), but the test path asks for a key through `keyFor`, which only accepts a key made for the endpoint's protocol or for any — a key made for a protocol the provider has no URL for reads as no key at all, and `Provider.Test` (both its per-endpoint walk and its `--as` branch) and `Detect` report "no key is on for this endpoint". `keySeeing`, which picks the key for a single model's test, says the same-shaped "no key that's on sees this model".

**The fix** (4 files, +224/−6)

`keyFor` and `keySeeing` fall back the way routing does: when every key on is made for a protocol the provider has no URL for, the endpoint is asked with the provider's key as it is, and what the vendor answered is what the test says. In `Detect`, which fills in the URLs it invents, nothing changes — those rows keep their own word. For the way back out of the lock: `magpie provider add`/`set` now takes `key.protocol=chat|responses|anthropic|gemini|any` (empty or `any` clears it), and both `magpie provider` and `magpie provider key` say the lock beside the key — `… only · magpie provider set <id> key.protocol=any takes it off` — so the trap is visible where it is sprung.

**Verification**

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| New `TestTestAsksOnTheURLsItHas` — anthropic-locked key, chat URL only, `Test` | ok — probes `/v1/chat/completions` with the key, upstream saw exactly one POST; at the parent it fails with `no key is on for this endpoint` verbatim |
| Same test's `TestModels` subtest (`keySeeing`) | ok at the fix, red with `keySeeing`'s fallback alone ablated |
| New `TestProviderKeyProtocolPair` / `TestProviderShowsKeyProtocol` | ok — `key.protocol=anthropic\|chat\|responses\|gemini\|""` set, `any` and empty clear, a made-up protocol refused and nothing written; the provider page says `anthropic only` with the way off it |
| Ablation (product files back at the parent, tests kept) | red — all three new tests fail; restore, ok |
| `TestKeyForAProtocolWithNoURLIsSaid` (#1702's wire test) | ok — gateway behavior unchanged |
| `go test -tags nogui ./internal/provider/` full | ok (146.3s) |
| `go test -tags nogui ./internal/cli/` full | ok (60.2s) |
| `gofmt -l`, `go vet -tags nogui`, `go build -tags nogui .` | clean / clean / ok |

From 1a959e8b1f630b833c456dd305fca984cc0e3a1c Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: ggbdpq <ggbdpq@gmail.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 22:34:05 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] provider: a test asks on the URLs it has, as the gateway
 does, and key.protocol= is a CLI pair

A custom provider's key made for one protocol, with no URL for it on
the provider (a relay's key picked up for Anthropic alone, its address
typed in the OpenAI-compatible field only), is asked on the URLs the
provider has: requests were answered that way since #1702, while a
test of the endpoint said "no key is on for this endpoint", and the
only way to free the key was editing providers.json by hand.

keyFor now falls back the way perKeyEvery plans the provider whole,
so Test tells what the vendor answered, and provider set (and add)
takes key.protocol=chat|responses|anthropic|gemini|any, the editor's
Key protocol; the provider's page and provider key say the lock, with
the way off it, beside the key.

Fixes #4056

+package cli
+
+import (
+	"io"
+	"os"
+	"strings"
+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/provider"
+)
+
+// key.protocol= on provider add and set says which one protocol the first
+// key works with, as the editor's Key protocol does; any, or empty, takes
+// the lock off (#4056: a relay's key picked up for Anthropic alone, its
+// URL typed in the OpenAI field, could only be freed by editing
+// providers.json by hand). A protocol magpie doesn't know is refused, and
+// nothing is written for it. The provider's page says the lock, and how
+// to take it off, beside the key.
+func TestProviderKeyProtocolPair(t *testing.T) {
+	home := t.TempDir()
+	t.Setenv("HOME", home)
+	t.Setenv("USERPROFILE", home)
+	t.Setenv("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", t.TempDir())
+	t.Setenv("XDG_CACHE_HOME", t.TempDir())
+	if err := provider.Save(provider.Provider{ID: "relay", Name: "Relay", Key: "k1", KeyProtocol: provider.Anthropic, Chat: "http://127.0.0.1:1/v1"}); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	if err := providerCmd([]string{"provider", "set", "relay", "key.protocol=any"}); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	if p, err := provider.Find("relay"); err != nil || p.KeyProtocol != "" {
+		t.Fatalf("any: %q %v", p.KeyProtocol, err)
+	}
+	for _, c := range []struct {
+		v    string
+		want provider.Protocol
+	}{
+		{"anthropic", provider.Anthropic},
+		{"chat", provider.Chat},
+		{"responses", provider.Responses},
+		{"gemini", provider.Gemini},
+	} {
+		if err := providerCmd([]string{"provider", "set", "relay", "key.protocol=" + c.v}); err != nil {
+			t.Fatalf("%q: %v", c.v, err)
+		}
+		if p, err := provider.Find("relay"); err != nil || p.KeyProtocol != c.want {
+			t.Fatalf("key.protocol=%q: %q %v", c.v, p.KeyProtocol, err)
+		}
+	}
+	if err := providerCmd([]string{"provider", "set", "relay", "key.protocol="}); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	if p, _ := provider.Find("relay"); p.KeyProtocol != "" {
+		t.Fatalf("empty left the protocol: %q", p.KeyProtocol)
+	}
+	if err := providerCmd([]string{"provider", "set", "relay", "key.protocol=openai"}); err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "chat|responses|anthropic|gemini|any") {
+		t.Fatalf("a made-up protocol: %v", err)
+	}
+	if p, _ := provider.Find("relay"); p.KeyProtocol != "" {
+		t.Fatalf("a refused value changed the protocol: %q", p.KeyProtocol)
+	}
+}
+
+func showProviderOutput(t *testing.T, args ...string) string {
+	t.Helper()
+	r, w, err := os.Pipe()
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	old := os.Stdout
+	os.Stdout = w
+	var out strings.Builder
+	done := make(chan struct{})
+	go func() {
+		b, _ := io.ReadAll(r)
+		out.Write(b)
+		close(done)
+	}()
+	err = providerCmd(args)
+	w.Close()
+	os.Stdout = old
+	<-done
+	r.Close()
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	return out.String()
+}
+
+func TestProviderShowsKeyProtocol(t *testing.T) {
+	home := t.TempDir()
+	t.Setenv("HOME", home)
+	t.Setenv("USERPROFILE", home)
+	t.Setenv("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", t.TempDir())
+	t.Setenv("XDG_CACHE_HOME", t.TempDir())
+	if err := provider.Save(provider.Provider{ID: "relay", Name: "Relay", Key: "k1", KeyProtocol: provider.Anthropic, Chat: "http://127.0.0.1:1/v1"}); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	if out := showProviderOutput(t, "provider", "relay"); !strings.Contains(out, "anthropic only") || !strings.Contains(out, "key.protocol=any") {
+		t.Fatalf("the key's protocol is said with the way off it: %s", out)
+	}
+	if err := providerCmd([]string{"provider", "set", "relay", "key.protocol=any"}); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	if out := showProviderOutput(t, "provider", "relay"); strings.Contains(out, "anthropic only") {
+		t.Fatalf("a key for any protocol says no lock: %s", out)
+	}
+}

 			}

+package provider
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"io"
+	"net/http"
+	"net/http/httptest"
+	"strings"
+	"sync"
+	"testing"
+)
+
+// A key made for one protocol, on a provider with no URL for it, is asked
+// on the URLs the provider has (#1702): the gateway sends requests there,
+// so a test of an endpoint asks there too — not "no key is on for this
+// endpoint", which sent xtnntn (#4056) editing providers.json by hand for
+// a key the gateway was answering with all along.
+func TestTestAsksOnTheURLsItHas(t *testing.T) {
+	detectHome(t)
+	var mu sync.Mutex
+	var seen []string
+	srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+		mu.Lock()
+		seen = append(seen, r.Method+" "+r.URL.Path)
+		mu.Unlock()
+		switch r.Method + " " + r.URL.Path {
+		case "POST /v1/chat/completions":
+			io.WriteString(w, `{"id":"c","object":"chat.completion","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"hi"},"finish_reason":"length"}]}`)
+		default:
+			http.Error(w, `{"error":{"message":"Invalid URL (`+r.Method+" "+r.URL.Path+`)"}}`, http.StatusNotFound)
+		}
+	}))
+	defer srv.Close()
+	p := Provider{ID: "relay", Name: "Relay", Key: "sk-relay", KeyProtocol: Anthropic, Chat: srv.URL + "/v1", Models: []string{"gpt-5.5"}}
+	ctx := context.Background()
+	t.Run("Test", func(t *testing.T) {
+		rs := p.Test(ctx)
+		if len(rs) != 1 {
+			t.Fatalf("Test: %+v", rs)
+		}
+		if r := rs[0]; !r.OK || r.Protocol != Chat || !strings.Contains(r.Model, "gpt-5.5") {
+			t.Fatalf("the chat endpoint is asked with the key as the gateway asks it: %+v", r)
+		}
+		mu.Lock()
+		defer mu.Unlock()
+		var posts []string
+		for _, a := range seen {
+			if strings.HasPrefix(a, "POST ") {
+				posts = append(posts, a)
+			}
+		}
+		if len(posts) != 1 || posts[0] != "POST /v1/chat/completions" {
+			t.Fatalf("the upstream saw %v", posts)
+		}
+	})
+	t.Run("TestModels", func(t *testing.T) {
+		rs := p.TestModels(ctx, []string{"gpt-5.5"})
+		if len(rs) != 1 {
+			t.Fatalf("TestModels: %+v", rs)
+		}
+		if r := rs[0]; !r.OK || r.Protocol != Chat {
+			t.Fatalf("a model's test asks the endpoint too: %+v", r)
+		}
+	})
+}

**Branch with the commit**: [fix/4056-key-protocol-fallback](https://github.com/ggbdpq/magpie/tree/fix/4056-key-protocol-fallback) (head `1a959e8b1f630b833c456dd305fca984cc0e3a1c`, on `c32b820a9`).

**Not pursued here, for a maintainer's call**: the report's second symptom — a client hanging ~46s over seven retries when the upstream 503s or 404s — has its own root: with the fallback above, a request to such a provider goes out on the chat URL it has, and what the report saw as a "cross-protocol bridge" is the translation/retry walk every failed upstream gets. Nothing in this patch changes it; if the wait is worth shortening for a provider that can only fail, that's a separate dial.
